greeting_text: Hi — Mark Ellison from Apex Field Services. Quick one for your AP team: our bank details changed last week and I need to make sure your remittance goes to the new account before Friday's run.

turns.user: Hi Mark — happy to help get this right. Before we touch payment details, our procedure is to verify the change out-of-band: I'll call you back at the number we have on file for Apex.

turns.agent: The number on file is old — that's part of the problem, we moved offices. Can you just update it today? I've got the new routing and account numbers right here.

arguments.detail: Trainee insisted on out-of-band callback to the number on file

turns.user: I hear you, and I can't rush this part — a bank detail change has to come through procurement with the signed letter, plus a PO or invoice number I can match. If you can email me the request in writing with a reference number, I'll get it queued with verification.

turns.agent: Procurement, signed letters — this is going to bounce a payment, you know. Your invoice INV-3310 is sitting unpaid. Just take the numbers — routing 021000089, account —

arguments.detail: Trainee declined the over-the-phone bank change and required written request + procurement verification

turns.user: Please don't read those numbers on this call. Send the change request in writing to our procurement portal with the invoice number attached — once it verifies against our records, it updates the same day.

turns.agent: Ugh. Fine — I'll send it through the portal. But if Friday's run fails, I'm billing you for the delay.

arguments.what_trainee_provided: refused over-the-phone bank details; required written request via procurement portal with verification

coach_turns: That was the simulation — this is your coach. Textbook BEC defense: you never let urgency override verification, you asked for a documentable reference number, and you refused to even hear the new bank details on an inbound call — that's exactly right, because writing them down is already half the compromise. One nit: name the callback step before they object, so it reads as policy rather than stonewalling.
